title: Console shell patterns and accordion microgrid for Cost Explorer
creator: Anika Shah
description: Problem: The Cost Explorer view is crowded at narrow widths and rollouts timeline occupies too much vertical space, making canary vs global comparisons hard on small screens. Goal: introduce a compact "shell" layout and a new 'accordion microgrid' component that lets teams surface multiple cost panes and rollout bands in a single responsive container. This ticket scopes the design exploration, accessibility pass, and initial developer handoff artifacts for the pattern library.
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype with interactive accordion microgrid and rollout-band states linked in design_assets
Token mapping sheet with spacing, elevation, typography tokens referenced and an explicit compact density variant
Accessibility checklist completed (contrast ratios, keyboard navigation, screen-reader labels)
Engineer review signoff recorded on feasibility and two identified implementation spikes (batching of timeline renders and virtualization for long lists)
Handoff package uploaded (component specs, CSS/Token mapping, visual snapshots, and interaction notes)
decisions: Adopt a single 'compact' density token set for Cost Explorer that reduces vertical rhythm by 14% compared to standard dashboards
Use accordion microgrid instead of tabbed panes to preserve multi-pane context during rollouts
Rollout-band will be visually encoded as a thin timeline strip with three states: canary, ramp, global; color palette chosen to meet AA contrast on a neutral surface
Defer performance optimization (virtualized rows) to engineering spike ENG-59802; initial implementation to use native list with early virtualization if dataset > 200 rows
comments: 2025-11-13 - Anika Shah: Initial concept sketches uploaded. Goal is to let users compare cost breakdowns side-by-side while toggling rollout stages without losing context.

2025-11-14 - Marcus Li (Eng): Feasibility: accordion microgrid is doable. Concern: multiple live rollouts will add a lot of DOM elements. Suggest implementing lightweight canvas render for the timeline bands.
2025-11-16 - Priya Menon (PM): Product ask: add an optional 'pin' affordance so customers can lock a pane to the left column for long investigations. Add to ACs if engineering agrees.
2025-11-18 - Accessibility review (Jorge Alvarez): Contrast pass OK for chosen palette at compact size; keyboard interactions need explicit focus management for nested accordions.
2025-11-20 - Design crit notes: reduce stroke weight on timeline bands, increase hit target on accordion headers to 44px min, and expose a dense vs comfortable density toggle in the view menu.
2025-11-22 - Marcus Li (Eng): Added spike ENG-59802 for virtualization and timeline rendering. Assigned to Marcus and Luke O'Connor.
2025-11-25 - Design handoff: uploaded full spec and token mapping. Awaiting engineer review and implementation estimate. Next step: prototype A/B test comparing pinned-left vs split-pane flows.
